prize_parts.citation: for developing targeted protein degradation, by which small molecules recruit E3 ubiquitin ligases to destroy chosen proteins, from the PROTAC concept to the molecular basis of cereblon-mediated glue degraders

statement.case_for: Targeted protein degradation is a new chemical principle, event-driven induced proximity instead of occupancy-based inhibition, and it is supported by quantitative physical chemistry: ternary-complex cooperativity, degradation kinetics and structure-guided linker and ligand design. It also has the widest base of support at opening (ranked by all eight members, including by me), and the concept has been reproduced by many independent laboratories over more than two decades. The Crews/Deshaies and Handa pairing covers both the heterobifunctional strand and the molecular-glue strand, which explains why thalidomide-type drugs work.
statement.case_against: No degrader is approved yet, so clinical validation is incomplete, and three names leave out Sakamoto, Ciulli, Gray, Ito and Kim, so the credit allocation is contestable. The molecular-glue and PROTAC strands could be seen as two achievements, which would strain a three-person limit. In my own opening I placed biomolecular phase separation (B052) first, and I still think it is the strongest new concept of molecular organisation on the shortlist, but the colleagues' maturity objections are fair and I cannot dismiss them.

responses.point: Peter Brzezinski ranks nitrogenase (B006) first as a mechanism-rich account of a very hard reaction, and ranks phase separation fourth but flags possible earliness because many functional claims in vivo are contested.
responses.response: I agree that phase separation is the weakest on maturity, and that is the main reason I have moved my preferred configuration away from it. The distinction between true demixing and other assemblies in living cells is not settled, and I would not want the Committee to cite a physiological claim that the field has not yet earned. On nitrogenase, the structural and kinetic work is clearly mature, but its mechanism of N2 binding is still open, which is the same kind of unresolved core I would object to elsewhere. It also drew support from only four members at opening, so I see it as a credible alternative rather than the consensus choice.

responses.point: Heiner Linke ranks base editing (B029) first and proposes Liu alone, arguing that Liu's group made the decisive step for both cytosine and adenine editors and that this is the most defensible attribution.
responses.response: The chemical logic of base editing is attractive and the attribution to Liu is cleaner than for PROTACs. My reservation is that it is conceptually an engineering fusion of a deaminase onto a programmable nickase, built directly on the platform that the 2020 prize recognised, and that Nishida and Kondo's parallel Target-AID work complicates a Liu-only citation. I ranked it sixth for these reasons. I would want to hear whether the Committee thinks the principle is new enough, and I do not think a Liu-only prize is as safe as it looks if the Target-AID priority is argued.

responses.point: Johan Aqvist ranks targeted protein degradation first and argues that it is a genuinely new pharmacological principle with quantitatively testable chemistry, naming Crews, Deshaies and Handa to cover both the bifunctional and glue strands.
responses.response: I agree with the scientific case and with the Crews, Deshaies, Handa configuration, which I think is the best use of three slots, because Handa's cereblon work provides the mechanism that unifies the glue degraders. My qualification is that approved clinical benefit is still limited and that Ciulli's structure-guided VHL ligand design is what made rational degrader design possible, so the citation should be written around the concepts and mechanisms rather than the number of drugs. I would also ask whether the Committee is comfortable leaving out Sakamoto, who co-authored the first PROTAC demonstration.

responses.point: Daniel Aili ranks ionizable lipid nanoparticles (B016) first as the strongest case of a molecular design principle that reached medicine, with Cullis, Hope and Madden as the core, while noting the overlap with the 2023 Medicine prize.
responses.response: I share his view of the science, because pH-dependent charge and phase behaviour of the ionizable lipid is lipid physical chemistry in the sense I work in, and the clinical record is unusually strong. My worry is attribution, since the formulation concept, lipid optimisation and library work were done in separate academic and industrial groups, and any three names will be disputed by the others. That makes it a harder call than PROTACs, so I keep it as an alternative rather than my first choice.

uncertainties: Whether the absence of an approved PROTAC drug should delay recognition of targeted protein degradation or whether the independent confirmation and clinical pipeline are enough.
Whether the PROTAC and molecular-glue strands are one achievement or two, and whether Sakamoto and Ciulli can be excluded from a three-person citation.
Whether phase separation will be judged mature enough in the next few years, given the debate about in vivo relevance and about what counts as phase separation.
Whether the ionizable lipid nanoparticle credit can be split in a defensible way, and whether the 2023 Medicine prize makes it a poor fit.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile. I work in lipid self-assembly, which is close to B016 and to the physical chemistry behind B052, and I sit on the committee with Lund colleagues Heiner Linke and Peter Somfai, but I have no stated personal or institutional tie to any shortlisted candidate.
